what: Quick reference: a complete fixed-context SNP workflow
title: 01. Getting Started with terradish
code: library(terradish) library(terra) library(ggplot2) data(ohio_ponds)  # 1. Align individuals and ponds, then summarize equal-size allele counts. g <- factor(ohio_ponds$samples$pond, levels = ohio_ponds$ponds$pond) Y <- rowsum(ohio_ponds$snp, g, reorder = FALSE) Y <- Y[ohio_ponds$ponds$pond, , drop = FALSE] N <- 2 * as.numeric(table(g)) stopifnot(all(N == N[1])) S <- cov_from_biallelic(Y, N) / N[1]  # 2. Retain the full projected landscape, including the matrix between ponds. x <- c(unwrap(ohio_ponds$covariates), unwrap(ohio_ponds$forest500)) graph <- conductance_surface(scale_covariates(x), ohio_ponds$ponds[c("x", "y")],   directions = 8, saveStack = TRUE)  # 3. Fit uniform and forest models; nu is an assumption, not the SNP count. control <- NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 200, ctol = 1e-8, ftol = 1e-8) fit0 <- terradish(S ~ 1, graph, measurement_model = wishart_covariance,   nu = 40, optimizer = "bfgs", control = control) fit <- terradish(S ~ forest500, graph, measurement_model = wishart_covariance,   nu = 40, optimizer = "bfgs", control = control)  # 4. Check convergence and compare; then read the coefficient as a ratio. aic_table(list(fit0, fit), mod_names = c("uniform", "forest500"))  # converged, Delta_AIC summary(fit)           # log-conductance coefficient and nuisance parameters exp(coef(fit))         # conductance ratio per SD of forest context exp(confint(fit))      # 95% interval for that ratio plot(fit, type = "marginal", data = graph)  # conductance across forest values maps <- plot(fit, type = "surface", data = graph) C <- conductance(graph, fit) map_limits <- range(terra::values(C), na.rm = TRUE)  # Keep all cells and share limits across the estimate and both bounds. for (p in maps) {   print(p + scale_fill_viridis_c(     trans = "log10", limits = map_limits,     breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20),     name = "Conductance\n(log color scale)"   )) }

title: 04. Model Comparison and Selection in terradish
code: library(terradish) library(terra) data(ohio_ponds) g <- factor(ohio_ponds$samples$pond, levels = ohio_ponds$ponds$pond) N <- 2 * as.numeric(table(g)) S <- cov_from_biallelic(rowsum(ohio_ponds$snp, g, reorder = FALSE)[ohio_ponds$ponds$pond, , drop = FALSE], N) / N[1] x <- c(unwrap(ohio_ponds$covariates), unwrap(ohio_ponds$forest500)) graph <- conductance_surface(scale_covariates(x), ohio_ponds$ponds[c("x", "y")],   directions = 8) f <- list(uniform = S ~ 1, forest = S ~ forest500,           forest_slope = S ~ forest500 + slope,           full = S ~ forest500 + slope + elevation) ctl <- NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 200, ctol = 1e-8, ftol = 1e-8)  # 1. Fit each declared candidate; use the multiple-start audit above in practice. fits <- lapply(f, function(z) terradish(z, graph,   measurement_model = wishart_covariance, nu = 40, optimizer = "bfgs", control = ctl))  # 2. Rank fits; 'converged' must be TRUE. Models within 2 AIC units have #    comparable support, unless the larger one only adds a parameter that #    leaves the log-likelihood almost unchanged (an uninformative parameter). aic_table(fits, mod_names = names(fits)) anova(fits$forest, fits$full)   # do slope and elevation add anything?  # 3. Score the same held-out ponds with all training parameters held fixed. cv <- terradish_cv_folds(graph, f, ohio_ponds$ponds$fold,   model = wishart_covariance, nu = 40, nuisance = "fixed",   optimizer = "bfgs", control = ctl) cv$results   # per-block held-out log-likelihood; larger is better cv$summary   # totals, shortfall from the best model, and its standard error

Preserve every start's status. defaults <- attr(smooth_loglinear_conductance(~ s(forest500, df = 3), surface$x),                  "default") spline_fits <- lapply(c(-0.5, 0, 0.5), function(start) {   theta <- defaults   theta[] <- start   tryCatch(terradish(S ~ s(forest500, df = 3), surface,     conductance_model = smooth_loglinear_conductance,     measurement_model = wishart_covariance, nu = 40, theta = theta,     optimizer = "bfgs", control = control), error = identity) }) valid <- vapply(spline_fits, function(z) !inherits(z, "error") &&   isTRUE(z$convergence$code == 0) && isTRUE(z$fit$subproblem$convergence == 0), logical(1)) likelihood <- vapply(spline_fits, function(z)   if (inherits(z, "error")) NA_real_ else as.numeric(logLik(z)), numeric(1)) data.frame(start = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5), valid, logLik = likelihood) #>   start valid   logLik #> 1  -0.5  TRUE 143.5772 #> 2   0.0  TRUE 143.5772 #> 3   0.5  TRUE 143.5772 if (!any(valid)) stop("No converged spline candidate") eligible <- which(valid) fit_spline <- spline_fits[[eligible[which.max(likelihood[valid])]]] summary(fit_spline) #> Conductance surface with 10404 vertices (24 focal) estimated by maximum likelihood #> Call:   terradish(formula = S ~ s(forest500, df = 3), data = surface, #>     conductance_model = smooth_loglinear_conductance, measurement_model = wishart_covariance, #>     nu = 40, theta = theta, optimizer = "bfgs", control = control) #> #> Loglikelihood: 143.5772 (5 degrees freedom) #> AIC: -277.1545 #> #> Number of function calls: 35 #> Number of optimization steps: 12 #> Convergence: converged | projected gradient: 2.03e-09 #> Norm of gradient at MLE: 2.785586e-09 #> #> Nuisance parameters (conditional on fitted conductance surface; measurement-model scale): #>        Estimate  Std. code: library(terradish) library(terra) data(ohio_ponds) # 0. Pond covariance from SNP dosage, with ponds in their declared order. g <- factor(ohio_ponds$samples$pond, levels = ohio_ponds$ponds$pond) Y <- rowsum(ohio_ponds$snp, g, reorder = FALSE) Y <- Y[ohio_ponds$ponds$pond, , drop = FALSE] N <- 2 * as.numeric(table(g)) S <- cov_from_biallelic(Y, N) / N[1] x <- c(unwrap(ohio_ponds$covariates), unwrap(ohio_ponds$forest500)) graph <- conductance_surface(scale_covariates(x), ohio_ponds$ponds[c("x", "y")]) ctl <- NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 200, ctol = 1e-8, ftol = 1e-8)  # 1. Spatial context is fixed; the spline estimates response shape. fit <- terradish(S ~ s(forest500, df = 3), graph,   conductance_model = smooth_loglinear_conductance,   measurement_model = wishart_covariance, nu = 40, optimizer = "bfgs", control = ctl) summary(fit)   # check Convergence; spline shape is reported before Coefficients  # 2. Interpret the whole curve, including its supported range. plot(fit, type = "marginal", data = graph) plot(fit, type = "marginal", data = graph, support = "focal")  # 3. Compare prediction with a simpler log-linear shape. Scores use only #    pairs within each held-out block; prefer the simpler shape on a tie. cv <- terradish_cv_folds(graph,   list(linear = S ~ forest500, spline = S ~ s(forest500, df = 3)),   ohio_ponds$ponds$fold, model = wishart_covariance, nu = 40,   conductance_model = list(linear = loglinear_conductance,                            spline = smooth_loglinear_conductance),   nuisance = "fixed", optimizer = "bfgs", control = ctl) cv$summary   # within_one_se is a descriptive tie flag, not a decision

code: # \donttest{ data(melip) forestcover <- terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover) coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)  # Name the layer, but do not scale it: the Gaussian model smooths the raw # raster first and then standardizes internally. names(forestcover) <- "forestcover"  # Coarsened so the example runs quickly: the raster is re-smoothed at every # candidate sigma. Use the full resolution in a real analysis. forestcover <- terra::aggregate(forestcover, fact = 3, na.rm = TRUE)  # Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell). The # cells of a twice-coarser grid are used so that the coarse-raster warm # start below also has one site per cell. coarse <- terra::aggregate(forestcover, fact = 2, na.rm = TRUE) keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(coarse, terra::crds(coords))) Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep] surface <- conductance_surface(forestcover, coords[keep], saveStack = TRUE)  gaussian_model <- gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(surface) fit <- terradish(   Fst ~ forestcover,   data = surface,   conductance_model = gaussian_model,   measurement_model = mlpe,   optimizer = "auto" )  # coef() holds the log-conductance coefficient (per SD of the smoothed # layer) and sigma.forestcover, the smoothing scale in map units (degrees # for these unprojected rasters). coef(fit) #>       forestcover sigma.forestcover  #>         0.3276100         0.2795342  # Roughly 111 km per degree near the equator converts the scale to km. gaussian_scale_summary(fit, distance_per_map_unit = 111,                        distance_unit = "km") #>     covariate     sigma sigma_lower sigma_upper sigma_internal sigma_conversion #> 1 forestcover 0.2795342      0.0675        1.17       2.070624            0.135 #>   sigma_conversion_mode native_unit sigma_cells_x sigma_cells_y  axis_50 #> 1                  cell     degrees      2.070624      2.070624 0.188543 #>   radial_50  axis_95 radial_95 sigma_km sigma_lower_km sigma_upper_km #> 1 0.3291264 0.547877  0.684229  31.0283         7.4925         129.87 #>   axis_50_km radial_50_km axis_95_km radial_95_km #> 1   20.92827     36.53303   60.81434     75.94941 plot(fit, type = "sigma", distance_per_map_unit = 111,      distance_unit = "km")   # On a full-resolution raster, a coarse-raster warm start cuts the cost of # the scale search. With exact_refine = TRUE the reported fit is refined # back on the original graph, so the estimates stay exact. fit_coarse <- terradish(   Fst ~ forestcover,   data = surface,   conductance_model = gaussian_model,   measurement_model = mlpe,   approximation = "coarse_raster",   approximation_control = list(factor = 2, exact_refine = TRUE),   optimizer = "auto" ) # }

code: library(terra)  data(melip) covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),                 terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)) coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords) names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover") # Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale. covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,                                                 na.rm = TRUE)) # Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell). keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords))) coords <- coords[keep] Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep] surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)  # Graph covariance (generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian) among the # focal sites under uniform conductance (all coefficients zero). laplacian_inv <- terradish_distance(theta = matrix(0, 1, 2),                                     formula = ~ forestcover + altitude,                                     data = surface,                                     covariance = TRUE)$covariance[, , 1]  # Generate an admissible squared-distance response from a positive # definite covariance, then evaluate the likelihood at known values. set.seed(1) Sigma <- 0.8 * laplacian_inv + 0.2 * diag(nrow(laplacian_inv)) observed_covariance <- rWishart(1, df = 40, Sigma = Sigma)[, , 1] / 40 observed_squared_distance <- dist_from_cov(observed_covariance) check_distance_response(observed_squared_distance)$admissible #> [1] TRUE value <- generalized_wishart(laplacian_inv, observed_squared_distance,                              nu = 40,                              phi = c(tau = 0.8, sigma = log(0.2))) value$objective  # negative log-likelihood; sigma is the LOG nugget #> [1] -23.55683

code: library(terra)  data(melip) covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),                 terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)) coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords) names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover") # Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale. covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,                                                 na.rm = TRUE)) # Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell). keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords))) coords <- coords[keep] Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep] surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)  # Graph covariance (generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian) among the # focal sites under uniform conductance (all coefficients zero). laplacian_inv <- terradish_distance(theta = matrix(0, 1, 2),                                     formula = ~ forestcover + altitude,                                     data = surface,                                     covariance = TRUE)$covariance[, , 1]  # Without 'phi': starting values and bounds for the nuisance parameters mlpe(laplacian_inv, Fst) #> $phi #>       alpha        beta         tau         rho  #>  0.01002299  0.22923592  6.47733469 -1.38629436  #>  #> $lower #> [1] -Inf    0 -Inf -Inf #>  #> $upper #> [1] Inf Inf Inf Inf #>  # With 'phi': the negative log-likelihood and derivatives at those values. # qlogis(2 * 0.2) sets the actual shared-site correlation to 0.2. value <- mlpe(laplacian_inv, Fst,               phi = c(alpha = 0, beta = 0.5, tau = -0.1,                       rho = qlogis(2 * 0.2))) value$objective #>       tau  #> -58.01211

code: # \donttest{ data(melip) covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),                 terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)) coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords) names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover") # Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale. covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,                                                 na.rm = TRUE)) # Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell). keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords))) coords <- coords[keep] Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep] surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)  # site-level altitude, turned into a pairwise |difference| IBE predictor site_altitude <- data.frame(   altitude = terra::extract(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude), coords)[, 2]) g_joint <- mlpe_covariates(site_altitude)  # joint isolation by environment and isolation by resistance fit_joint <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface,                        conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,                        measurement_model = g_joint)  # Expected change in genetic distance across the covariate's 10th-to-90th # percentile spread, on the response scale rather than the log scale. change <- mlpe_response_change(fit_joint) change #>          covariate        low      high  contrast   estimate   conf.low #> 1 absdiff_altitude 0.02037562 0.5275703 0.5071947 0.03288384 0.02661041 #>    conf.high conf.level #> 1 0.03915727       0.95  # A narrower, interquartile contrast mlpe_response_change(fit_joint, probs = c(0.25, 0.75)) #>          covariate     low      high  contrast   estimate   conf.low  conf.high #> 1 absdiff_altitude 0.08377 0.3477135 0.2639435 0.01711271 0.01384802 0.02037739 #>   conf.level #> 1       0.95 # }

title: Print and read a settings assessment — print.terradish_setting_assessment
text: read output.  comes four parts. Graph reports size problem: vertices (active raster cells), edges, focal sites, conductance parameters.  number decides whether rest matters.  roughly 50,000 vertices defaults almost always fine; hundred thousand, solver choice dominates runtime. Recommended settings lists optimizer, line search, solver, approximation probes favored, followed parenthesized reason. Pass straight fit <- terradish(..., optimizer = rec$optimizer, control = rec$control, solver = rec$solver), rec <- assessment$recommended.  choices change computational path, never estimates. Defaults comparison one-line verdict: whether assessment agreed package defaults.  says matched, nothing can drop assessment script. Probes measurements behind recommendation.  optimizer table gives elapsed time log-likelihood candidate reached probe budget, candidate fast reaches worse log-likelihood actually better.  solver table shows three fastest direct factorizations split setup solve time; setup dominates fit re-factorizes often, solve time focal set large.  Notes collects anything needs attention, solver failed converge probing.

Scaling avoids numeric overflow # and makes each coefficient a per-standard-deviation effect. names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover") covariates <- scale_covariates(covariates)  # A few melip sites share a raster cell; keep one site per cell. keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords))) coords <- coords[keep] Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]  # Build the graph (eight neighbors by default). surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)  # MLPE (the default) accounts for pairs that share a sampling site. fit_mlpe <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface,                       measurement_model = mlpe) fit_mlpe$convergence$code   # 0 means converged; check before reading on #> [1] 0 summary(fit_mlpe) #> Conductance surface with 22443 vertices (34 focal) estimated by maximum likelihood #> Call:   terradish(formula = Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface,  #>     measurement_model = mlpe) #>  #> Loglikelihood: 1825.936 (6 degrees freedom) #> AIC: -3639.873  #>  #> Number of function calls: 22  #> Number of optimization steps: 6  #> Convergence: converged | projected gradient: 4.82e-08  #> Norm of gradient at MLE: 6.341795e-08  #>  #> Nuisance parameters (conditional on fitted conductance surface; measurement-model scale): #>        Estimate  Std. code: # \donttest{ library(terra)  data(melip) covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),                 terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)) coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords) names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover") # Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale. covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,                                                 na.rm = TRUE)) # Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell). keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords))) Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep] surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords[keep]) conductance_model <- loglinear_conductance(~ altitude + forestcover, surface$x)  # One evaluation at theta = (-0.3, 0.3): negative log-likelihood, its # gradient and Hessian with respect to theta, and the profiled nuisance # parameters. value <- terradish_algorithm(conductance_model, leastsquares,                              surface, Fst, theta = c(-0.3, 0.3)) value$objective #> [1] -1375.273 value$gradient #> [1] -94.60471  51.19362 value$phi #>              [,1] #> alpha -0.01942733 #> beta   0.31180555 #> tau    6.91515095 # }

Use the full resolution in a real analysis. covariates <- terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3, na.rm = TRUE)  # Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell). keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords))) Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]  # Express the bounds in map units, using the coarsened cell width. cell_width <- mean(terra::res(covariates)) # A 2-point grid over two layers is 4 # candidate fits; use a wider grid in practice. fit_scale <- terradish_scale_optim(   Fst ~ altitude + forestcover,   covariates = covariates,   coords = coords[keep],   lower = cell_width,   upper = 6 * cell_width,   search = "grid",   grid_points = 2,   measurement_model = leastsquares,   optimizer = "bfgs" ) fit_scale$par          # selected smoothing scale per layer, in map units #>    altitude forestcover  #>       0.135       0.135  fit_scale$value        # objective value there (lower is better) #> [1] -2748.498 fit_scale$objective    # which objective was minimized ("aic" by default) #> [1] "aic" fit_scale$evaluations  # every candidate tried, with its AIC and loglik #>   altitude forestcover objective       aic   loglik status #> 1    0.135       0.135 -2748.498 -2748.498 1381.249     OK #> 2    0.810       0.135 -2743.431 -2743.431 1378.716     OK #> 3    0.135       0.810 -2728.719 -2728.719 1371.360     OK #> 4    0.810       0.810 -2726.710 -2726.710 1370.355     OK coef(fit_scale$fit)    # conductance coefficients at the selected scale #>    altitude forestcover  #>  -0.2419000   0.2382399  # }
